site.name: Skyhop
site.title: Skyhop: hand your Claude Code session to the cloud, and get it back
site.description: Skyhop is a plugin for Claude Code. Type /skyhop and your running session moves to the cloud with its code and full history. Carry on from claude.ai/code or the Claude app, and it comes home as the same session.

how.heading: One command to leave, none to come back

steps.title: Hand off.
steps.body: Type /skyhop. Skyhop shows the plan, with the branch, what will be uploaded and the permission mode, and asks before anything leaves your machine.

steps.title: Carry on anywhere.
steps.body: The cloud chat opens with your last 50 exchanges as real messages, word for word, and carries on from there. Reply from claude.ai/code or the Claude app on your phone.

steps.title: Come home.
steps.body: Quit the window, open claude in the same repository, pick the session in /resume and send a message. The cloud's messages are in it, and the cloud's code is in your files.

how.after: Hand off again later, even a day later, and it goes back to the same cloud chat.

diagram.key: Key goes straight to the cloud chat's first message, never through GitHub

safety.heading: Built to leave your repository alone

cards.title: Your checkout stays as it was.
cards.body: Your branch, working tree and index are unchanged.

cards.title: Nothing is force-pushed.
cards.body: Skyhop only creates its own skyhop branches.

cards.title: Secrets stop the handoff.
cards.body: If the scan finds a likely secret, nothing leaves your machine.

cards.title: Your conversation is encrypted on GitHub.
cards.body: AES-256-GCM, and the key is never pushed.

cards.title: You confirm first.
cards.body: You see the branch, remote, changes and upload before anything is sent.

cards.title: Coming home never overwrites.
cards.body: If your files changed, the cloud's code waits on its own branch.

safety.footnote: The secret scan matches known patterns, so it can miss things.

items.q: Does the cloud chat show my whole conversation?
items.a: It shows your last 50 exchanges as real messages, and --history changes that, up to 200. The cloud session itself has the full history. Turn on Remote Control before handing off to also get a link to the whole conversation.

items.q: Will I see Claude's tool activity live?
items.a: No. You get a progress line about every 100 seconds, then the reply with a list of the steps it took.

items.q: Does it use more of my plan?
items.a: No, about the same as working locally. The cloud session's replies are shown as written, so nothing is generated twice. Only if the cloud chat can't get ready and falls back to a recap does the chat repeat each reply, on Haiku to keep it cheap.
Your conversation and memory notes are. Your code isn't, so on a public repository the skyhop code branches are public too.

items.q: What if I typed on my laptop while the cloud kept going?
items.a: The cloud part becomes a separate session, and yours stays as it was.

items.q: How long can one message run?
Which systems does it run on?
items.a: macOS and Windows. On Windows the project needs a GitHub remote, because Skyhop hands off through GitHub there. Linux hasn't been tested with a real handoff yet.

items.q: Can I go back to the same cloud chat later?
items.a: Yes. Hand the session off again and it returns to its earlier chat, even a day later. Use /skyhop --new-chat to start a fresh one.
No. It's an independent plugin for Claude Code.
